assumptions: Carter static candidate v2: chassis-local deck height derives from measured118 chassis collision AABB top plus an authored2mm mounting gap, existing post height and deck half thickness. This AABB is not a mechanical surface or strength certificate.
Original generic bolted-deck/raised-support candidate, not a manufacturer model, certified payload or finished low-profile lifting AMR.
All dimensions, masses, uniform material distributions, friction and contact settings are authored development assumptions, not measurements.

Nova Carter remains the development base. Declared keepouts below are candidate integration constraints, not its measured collider/sensor geometry. Actual robot-frame transform, body/sensor clearance, mount strength, added inertia and navigation footprint need native admission before installation.
Existing presentation-only cargo is independent. This profile does not change a registry, scene, map, footprint, controller or sensor.

Probe uses fixed stand pads instead of a robot chassis. Carrier and tote are separate dynamic compound bodies; centred ballast is rigidly included in tote inertia, not loose contents. Separation is an authored upward velocity impulse, not a lift actuator or unloading operation.
